title: The Quantum Electron Cloud of a drug-like molecule

provenance.source: Reference video supplied by the channel owner (downloaded from Facebook, 720x1280).
provenance.method: 24 frames sampled evenly (one every 2.5 s) plus full-size stills; scene timing is accurate to about 1.5 s.
provenance.audio_finding: Music only: speech recognition found no speech.
unreadable: The subtitle under 'Change one group, X' was mid-fade in every sampled frame.
provenance.reuse: Use as a style and structure reference. Every number in it comes from a real calculation; a remake needs its own calculation, not these numbers copied.

builder_instructions: Recreate a 60 s vertical 3D explainer built on a real density-functional calculation. One molecule stays centre stage and changes representation: ball-and-stick, electron point cloud, density isosurface, electrostatic-potential surface, frontier orbitals, then two substituted variants. A centred title and subtitle change per chapter; a panel under the molecule shows the equation, plot or energy diagram for that chapter. The last chapter states the limits of the method. No narration.

intent.goal: Show what an electron density is, how DFT computes it, and what substituents do to frontier orbitals.
intent.audience: Undergraduate chemistry and physics students, science enthusiasts.
intent.takeaway: A molecule is a cloud of electron density; computed orbital energies describe it but do not predict a drug's effect.

science.how_to_reproduce: Write a lab script that runs the calculation (PySCF needs Linux or macOS), exports cube files for the density, ESP and orbitals, and prints every number above; the ledger then checks each on-screen value against the script.

lines_appearing_in_order: Orbital energies and the gap depend on the functional and basis set (here B3LYP/6-31G*).
They are model-dependent descriptors — not predictions of potency, binding or clinical efficacy. (amber)
The molecule is a hypothetical scaffold, computed in the gas phase, at one geometry.
Electrons are computed. Efficacy is measured. (bold)
